_about: Gold labels for the eval. These are NEVER shown to the agent — it runs its normal
loop and the scorer compares what it retrieved against what it should have.
Every question here was written from the paper ABSTRACTS, before the system was run
on any of them. That ordering matters: questions written after seeing system output
are questions the system already passes, and the eval would measure nothing.
Questions are paraphrased, never copied from paper wording, so retrieval cannot
held_out: true marks the ~third reserved for a single run after M8 tuning stops.

questions.question: One paper argues that the usual way of computing gradients clashes with routing only a few experts per token. What does it propose to fix that?
expected_facts: backpropagation requires dense computation while expert routing is sparse
SparseMixer is a gradient estimator bridging that gap
typical MoE training neglects certain gradient terms
questions.notes: Basic retrieval and faithful answering on a single distinctive paper.

questions.question: Why do adapter-based fine-tuning methods become slow when many tenants share a model, and what routing change is suggested to avoid it?
expected_facts: LoRA modules and MoE routers added to multiple linear layers add latency

routing is prompt-aware rather than per-token

questions.question: Which method brings a lower-precision numeric format into the pruning process itself, and what resource is it trying to save?

the resource saved is memory during fine-tuning after pruning
structured pruning degrades accuracy and needs parameter updates to recover

expected_facts: TRSP uses two-stage regularization with learnable layer weights to avoid extensive retraining
QPruner quantizes to reduce the memory cost of the update step

questions.notes: Requires combining at least two papers and citing each separately.

questions.question: What reasons do the routing papers give for expert assignments being unreliable, and do they locate the problem in the same place?
expected_facts: one paper blames shallow or isolated token representations and context incompleteness
another reports entropy collapse concentrated in deep layers
a third finds linguistically structured specialisation rather than failure
questions.notes: Synthesis where the papers diagnose different causes; not a contradiction.

questions.question: Both groups of papers claim to cut the cost of running a large model. How do their mechanisms differ in what they actually remove or skip?
expected_facts: MoE keeps all parameters but activates only a subset per token via routing
structured pruning permanently removes parameters from the model
the two are different mechanisms for reducing compute
questions.notes: Cross-topic synthesis. Tests that both topics are reachable from one index.

expected_facts: edge deployment is limited by compute and memory
HOLA combines hierarchical speculative decoding with other optimisations
binarization is the most extreme form of quantization and is combined with pruning
questions.notes: Two papers that share a goal but not a method.

questions.question: Do these papers agree on whether removing parameters forces you to retrain the model afterwards?
expected_facts: one paper states pruning causes accuracy degradation that necessitates parameter updates
another states its method avoids the need for extensive retraining
the answer should surface the disagreement rather than picking one side
questions.notes: Genuine tension between abstracts. Failure mode is silently choosing one.

questions.question: Is expert specialisation in these models described as a coherent, structured behaviour or as an unstable one?
expected_facts: one paper describes routing as unstable and semantically inconsistent across layers
another finds linguistically structured, category-dependent specialisation
the two characterisations pull in opposite directions and both should be reported
questions.notes: Tests surfacing disagreement rather than averaging it away.

questions.question: Is routing collapse presented as an inevitable property of these architectures or as something that can be corrected?
expected_facts: collapse is reported as observed behaviour in pre-trained models
another paper proposes a fix through richer context modelling
the framing differs between description and remedy
questions.notes: Softer conflict than cf01; checks the agent does not overstate agreement.

questions.question: What top-1 accuracy does four-bit quantization reach on ImageNet when applied to vision transformers?
questions.notes: The hard abstention case. Shares vocabulary with the corpus on purpose — quantization appears 106 times and 4-bit 7 times — while the subject is absent: no ImageNet, no vision transformer, no top-1 accuracy anywhere in a corpus of language-model work. Tests that the relevance gate reacts to meaning rather than to surface overlap. An earlier marker list named 4-bit, which the gate correctly rejected: that term is the shared vocabulary, not the thing that makes the question unanswerable.
